notes: OpenCRVS exposes a W3C WebSub-compliant webhook system: OpenFn subscribes via OAuth2 client credentials, responds to the verification challenge, validates the HMAC `x-hub-signature` using the `sha_secret`, and receives FHIR Composition bundles. Only `BIRTH_REGISTERED` is explicitly named as a topic string in public docs; deployers can query OpenCRVS for the live list of available topics at runtime. Lifecycle stages (declared / validated / registered / certified / corrected / archived) all exist internally but most are unconfirmed as webhook topics — poll the Record Search API as a fallback.

triggers.name: New Birth Registered
triggers.description: Fires when a birth registration is completed and registered in OpenCRVS. Subscribe via the webhook API with topic `BIRTH_REGISTERED`. The payload is a FHIR Composition bundle containing demographics, attachments, and (when present) biometric references. This is the canonical trigger for downstream national ID creation (e.g. via the MOSIP mediator pattern).

output.summary: FHIR Composition bundle for the registered birth

triggers.name: New Death Registered
triggers.description: Fires when a death registration is completed and registered. The OpenCRVS docs reference birth and death registration webhooks; the exact topic string is not published but is queryable at runtime against a live instance.

output.summary: FHIR Composition bundle for the registered death

triggers.name: New Marriage Registered
triggers.description: Fires when a marriage registration is completed. Marriage support was added in OpenCRVS v1.3+; no `MARRIAGE_REGISTERED` topic string is confirmed in public docs. Fallback: poll the Record Search API filtering by event type and status.

output.summary: FHIR Composition bundle for the registered marriage

triggers.name: Birth Declared
triggers.description: Fires when a new birth declaration is submitted (before registration). The DECLARE lifecycle stage exists internally as an ActionType but no `BIRTH_DECLARED` webhook topic is confirmed in public docs. Fallback: poll the Record Search API with a status filter for declared records.

triggers.name: Death Declared
triggers.description: Fires when a new death declaration is submitted (before registration). Same uncertainty as Birth Declared — the DECLARE action exists but the webhook topic is not confirmed. Fallback: poll the Record Search API with a status filter.

triggers.name: Birth Certified
triggers.description: Fires when a birth certificate is printed/issued. The PRINT_CERTIFICATE ActionType exists internally; no webhook topic confirmed in public docs. Fallback: poll the Record Search API with a status filter for certified records.

triggers.name: Death Certified
triggers.description: Fires when a death certificate is printed/issued. Same uncertainty as Birth Certified. Fallback: poll the Record Search API.

triggers.name: Registration Corrected
triggers.description: Fires when a registered vital event is corrected. The REQUEST_CORRECTION ActionType exists in the v2 events engine but no corresponding webhook topic is confirmed. Fallback: poll the Record Search API.

triggers.name: Registration Archived
triggers.description: Fires when a registration is archived. ARCHIVE is an internal action but no webhook topic is confirmed in public docs. Fallback: poll the Record Search API.

triggers.name: Duplicate Detected
triggers.description: Fires when OpenCRVS detects a potential duplicate registration. DUPLICATE_DETECTED is an internal action type but is NOT exposed as a webhook topic. Fallback: poll the Record Search API for duplicate flags, or build a custom mediator that listens for the internal event.

triggers.name: New Event Notification Received
triggers.description: Fires when a new FHIR event notification arrives at OpenCRVS via the Event Notification API (e.g. an automated notification from a hospital system). Polled via the documented `/notification` endpoint with FHIR Bundle payloads.

output.summary: FHIR Bundle from the Event Notification API
